name: West Virginia v EPA
description: Petition by 19 States (led by West Virginia) and coal-sector companies against the EPA challenging the breadth of the agency’s regulatory powers under Section 111(d) of the Clean Air Act, in particular the possibility of imposing “generation shifting” (shifting of electricity generation from coal to lower-emission sources), already the basis of the Obama-era Clean Power Plan.
outcome: 6–3 judgment in favour of the petitioners. The United States Supreme Court, expressly applying the “major questions doctrine” for the first time, held that Congress had not given the EPA clear authorisation to impose systemic transformations of such magnitude on the electricity sector, and that the EPA therefore cannot use Section 111(d) as the basis for such broad regulation. A setback for federal climate regulation, with knock-on effects on every broad regulatory delegation.
